items.title: Prototype opt-in signed cloud fan controls (design review)
items.body:
## Description

Concrete **draft for architecture review** for #2119: opt-in signed/encrypted cloud-MQTT fan controls, based on [Open Bamboo Networking](https://github.com/ClusterM/open-bamboo-networking)'s research. This is not ready for an in-process MIT merge; see the licensing and lifecycle blockers below and `SIGNING_DESIGN.md`.

The implementation adds local bundle validation, correlated `security.app_cert_install` provisioning, encrypted-only G-code, durable sequence allocation, session invalidation/reprovisioning, no automatic command replay, and authorization-gated native fan controls using printer telemetry.

A development build on ha-bambulab 2.2.25 / HA 2026.9.1 / ARM64 / X1C 01.12.00.00 passed a controlled chamber-fan **0 → 20 → 0%** test, with separate printer telemetry and restoration confirmed, while retaining Bambu Cloud and keeping Developer LAN Mode off. The owner also tested normal use. Other fan entities were exposed but not individually actuated in that controlled test. This branch ports the code to current `main`; it has been regression-tested, not installed over the working system.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Other (please describe): draft design/protocol reference, blocked on licensing and credential lifecycle

### Link to Issue

https://github.com/greghesp/ha-bambulab/issues/2119

Related extractor contribution: [BambuSlicerKeySaver #3](https://github.com/danielwoz/BambuSlicerKeySaver/pull/3).

The prerequisite fan fixes in #2120 merged on 6 September. This draft is now synchronized with current `main`; those fixes are no longer part of its feature diff.

## Documentation

- [x] I have updated the relevant documentation to reflect these changes
- [ ] No documentation updates were necessary for this change

`SIGNING_DESIGN.md` records features, evidence, credentials, failure modes, test commands and decisions needed before readiness.

## Testing

- [x] I have added/updated tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] All new and existing tests passed

- Current branch in an isolated temporary copy inside HA 2026.9.1's Python runtime: **140 passed** (`tests/pybambu` plus `tests/test_fan_entity.py`). No real MQTT connections or service calls.
- Generated RSA/certificate/CRL fixtures cover signature/encryption format, expiry/revocation, file permissions/symlinks, correlated provisioning, stale replies, restart-safe/concurrent IDs, own-command rejection, and telemetry rather than optimistic success.
- Optional entity tests skip when HA is absent; normal CI runs the pybambu suite.
- Source/privacy scanning and `git diff --check` passed. No private bundle or proprietary executable is supplied.

## Additional Notes — why this is a draft

1. **License:** new signing module, signing tests and validator are AGPL-3.0-only, with `COPYING.signing`; original MIT notices remain. I am not asking for a silent license change or asserting an AGPL/MIT boundary has been settled. Please advise whether a separately packaged signer, an AGPL fork, or another explicitly acceptable basis is preferred. A separate process alone is not a licensing conclusion.
2. **Renewal:** reconnect provisioning is implemented; vendor credential renewal, onboarding/repair UI and lifecycle ownership are not. No downloadable key store or bundled vendor credentials is proposed.
3. **Expired vendor CRL:** the hardware proof needed an explicitly reviewed, exact-bundle-pinned, maximum-30-day exception for an authentic but stale vendor CRL. Strict expiry is the default. This does not establish fresh revocation status, and automatic extension is not implemented or proposed. Maintainers should decide whether that policy is acceptable at all before readiness.
4. **Trust/coverage:** device-certificate validation, explicit opt-in, supported-model policy, full reconnect/reboot/rotation behavior and broader hardware coverage need design review.

Prepared with AI assistance; the protocol work is credited to its researchers and the hardware evidence is described narrowly. No logs, private identifiers, compatibility receipts, signing material or account credentials are included. Please treat this as a reviewable implementation of the proposal, not a promise of maintenance-free support or an immediate merge request.


### 7 September follow-up review

Resolved the conflicts after #2120 was squash-merged and preserved the newer upstream changes. Updated verification: **133 lightweight tests** and **140 tests in an isolated HA 2026.9.1 runtime** passed. `SIGNING_DESIGN.md` now identifies concrete readiness gaps: device-certificate chain/identity validation, explicit opt-in and onboarding/repair, the general `print` signing hook versus a fan-only boundary, and a supported credential/CRL lifecycle. These are still open; the PR remains a draft. No live installation or printer was changed by this branch synchronization.
